newsitem.title: FRANCE: French industry more bearish on jobs, investment.
newsitem.headline: French industry more bearish on jobs, investment.

text.p: French large company bosses expected recruitment to fall 0.1 percent in the 1996 second half from the first half and pared down expected rises in 1996 investment levels versus 1995 to nine percent from 12 percent, an INSEE national statistics institute survey said on Friday.
INSEE said in a statement its July survey showed large company bosses were "relatively pessimistic on the end of the year" on recruitment after a first-half rise of 0.1 percent.
On investment, the survey showed bosses in the manufacturing industry also revising lower investment increase expectations to nine percent from 13 percent when they were surveyed in January.
In cars and transport, it showed they expected a fall of one percent in investment versus their January prediction of a nine-percent rise.
But in services, bosses were expecting a slightly more significant rise than they were counting on back in January, a rise of 10 percent rather than nine percent.
In the wholesale inter-industry segment, they expected a rise of five percent in investment compared to expectations in January of a one-percent rise.
INSEE said its survey series had not been running long enough to allow for seasonal corrections, and the results should be read with caution for those reasons.
